merge.E1>G: Sticking to the way you've always done things, you haven't let in new people or new work, and meanwhile your energy has drained and your circle has thinned. Now you're worn out alone, with no strength to change and no one to lean on.
merge.E1>H: Things outside are already changing, but you're holding on to the familiar place, so each time change comes, it hits you unprepared. You're only being pushed along by the situation, and you haven't chosen a single thing yourself.
merge.E3>A: You kept reworking unfinished tasks, so you couldn't hand them off, and in the end every task stayed in your hands. Not one thing gets finished, and the work just keeps piling up.
merge.E3>B: As you fixed and refixed things to meet other people's standards, the answer you wanted never came. Reading the room and polishing over and over, you're worn out.
merge.E3>C: Reworking things because they're not done yet combines with waiting until “everything is in place,” so you're caught in a loop with no start and no finish. Only the list of fixes grows, and you haven't moved forward a single step.
merge.E3>D: The more you fix, the more the flaws stand out, and because you're afraid of looking lacking, you fix it again. You can neither put it out there nor drop it, and only the worry has grown.
merge.E3>E: On top of the habit of reworking without finishing, you now can't let go, so finishing has moved even further away. The longer you've held on, the heavier it's gotten, and still you can't put it down.
merge.E3>F: Endless polishing plus the pressure to finish fast has kept you circling the same spot without rest. For all the time you've put in, you have nothing to show for it, and that's made you even more impatient.
merge.E3>G: Reworking without end used up all your strength, so now there's no energy left even to touch it. Among the unfinished things, you've sunk down alone without being able to tell anyone.
merge.E3>H: The situation keeps changing, but you're still fixing the earlier work, so there's been no room to adjust to the new conditions. The world outside has moved ahead, and you've fallen behind, caught on work that isn't finished.
merge.E5>A: Even after saying you'd share the load this time, whenever things got busy or hard, you went back to doing it all yourself. In the end, the load sits on your shoulders alone, the same as before.
merge.E5>B: Even when you tried to say what you wanted, as soon as the mood got tense you went back to going along as before. Each time you turned back, the hurt you couldn't voice piled up a little more.
merge.E5>C: You start a new way, but when you're not sure, you go back to the old way, so the decision to change gets pushed to next time, every time. Going back and forth between starting and retreating, in the end you haven't decided anything.
merge.E5>D: Partway through changing, even one small setback makes you think “maybe it just won't work,” and that fear sends you back to the old way. So you're stuck halfway, neither changed nor the same as before.
merge.E5>E: Your habit of going back partway through changing shows up again now as not being able to let go, so the same pattern has doubled and set hard. All the effort you put into changing has gone nowhere, and you're right back where you started.
merge.E5>F: Frustrated that you couldn't change, you pushed yourself, and the harder you pushed, the more tired you got and the faster you slid back to the old way. Trying hard and falling apart again and again has only worn down your energy.
merge.E5>G: Repeatedly trying to change and then going back has worn you out, so now you have neither the strength to try again nor anyone to talk to. You're stalled in the same place, alone and drained.
merge.E5>H: The situation outside demands change, but whenever it's hard you go back to the old way, so the situation and your habits keep clashing. Caught between them, you can't go either way and just keep wavering.
merge.F1>A: While you ran without rest, you added other people's shares one by one, and since you never stopped, there was no chance to set anything down. The load you've shouldered alone has gone past what your body can handle.
merge.F1>B: You couldn't say you wanted to rest, so you've kept running at other people's pace. Now you're holding on, with the tiredness and the hurt piling up inside where no one can see.
merge.F1>C: Running nonstop left no time to stop and think things through, and the things that really mattered kept getting pushed back. You've been busy moving, but what you truly need to decide is still sitting there.
merge.F1>D: Afraid of falling behind if you stopped, you kept running, and the more you ran, the scarier resting became. Your body is worn out, but the worry won't let you stop.
merge.F1>E: Afraid of losing what you gained by running, you grip it tighter, and to protect what you're gripping, you run again. Unable to let go or rest, you're out of breath.
merge.F1>F: Your habit of running without rest meets the pressure you're putting on yourself right now, so you have even less room to stop. You're taking the same hit twice, and your body is wearing down all at once.
merge.F1>G: The price of running without rest was an empty tank, and being busy pulled you away from people too. Now even when you stop, you can't really rest, and no one is left by your side.
merge.F1>H: Outside schedules and demands kept coming at you, and you didn't stop running either, so you had no way to make time to rest. Chased by the situation and pushed by habit, you're worn out with no time to breathe.
merge.F2>A: Because you come down on yourself first when things are hard, “I'll just do more” comes out before “please help.” So the things you've taken on alone keep growing instead of shrinking.
merge.F2>B: Since you blame yourself first when problems come up, even things that hurt you became things you should just put up with. The more you swallow what you want to say, the louder the self-blame gets.
merge.F2>C: Because you've been so hard on yourself, you're extra careful not to get things wrong, and the more careful you are, the more decisions get put off. Then you scold yourself for putting them off and keep circling in place.
merge.F2>D: The more you push yourself, the bigger your clumsy side looks, and the more you fear it will be seen. In the end, you only count your shortcomings and can't take a single step.
merge.F2>E: Even as you scold yourself for not letting go, all that scolding keeps you chewing over what you did wrong back then. You're stuck between the past and your own self-blame.
merge.F2>F: Your habit of coming down on yourself first shows up again in how you're driving yourself right now, so you've never once let yourself rest. The pressure has doubled and is squeezing you with no room to breathe.
merge.F2>G: Pushing yourself every time things went wrong used up all your energy, and afraid that side of you would show, you started avoiding people too. So you're worn out and hiding alone.
merge.F2>H: You've blamed yourself even for things that went wrong because of outside circumstances. The more the situation blocks you, the more you blame yourself, so you're wearing yourself out alone in front of things you can't change.
merge.F3>A: Trying to stay on top of everything made handing things off feel risky, so in the end you did it all yourself. The tasks you couldn't let go of have piled up, and you're holding on alone.
merge.F3>B: Keeping everything from going wrong meant managing even the moods around you, and you pushed your own wishes to the back. On the outside things run smoothly, but inside you're full of words you've held back.
merge.F3>C: Since you can only move after weighing every possible case, you put off starting if even one thing is left to weigh. Your plans are thorough, but you haven't actually taken a step.
merge.F3>D: It felt like everything would fall apart if you missed one thing, so you held on to all of it, and the tighter you held, the more every small gap shook you. The more you tried to control things, the more the worry grew.
merge.F3>E: Used to keeping a tight grip on everything, you're now clutching what you have even harder for fear of losing it. It feels like everything would fall apart if you let go, so you're holding on with all your strength.
merge.F3>F: Your habit of controlling everything meets the pressure to get it done fast, so you haven't given yourself an inch of room to rest. You've taken care of everything, and you're the one who's worn out.
merge.F3>G: Managing everything used up all your energy, so even during your rest you keep running checks in your head. With no room left to see people, you're worn out alone.
merge.F3>H: You tried to have everything sorted with your own hands, but things outside didn't go according to plan. The more things happen that you can't help, the harder you try to grip, and you're only losing strength.
merge.F4>A: Wanting to finish fast, you'd often just do it yourself instead of waiting for others. Keeping up that pace alone, all the work and responsibility became yours and sit heavily on you.
merge.F4>B: You need results fast, but you're also reading the room, so your own pace always got pushed back. Impatience and holding back clash, so you're burning inside but can't say a word on the outside.
merge.F4>C: Remembering times you rushed and ruined things, you now wait until you're sure, but the longer you wait, the more impatient you get. Part of you wants to hurry and part of you keeps stalling, so you're stuck in place.
merge.F4>D: When results don't come fast, it feels like failure and the worry grows, and the more it grows, the more you rush. You picked up speed, but all you're left with is unease.
merge.F4>E: You can't let go of what you grabbed to get fast results, now that you're afraid of losing out. Letting go feels like wasting the time you've put in, but the tighter you hold, the longer your next step is delayed.
merge.F4>F: Your habit of rushing meets the pressure you're putting on yourself right now, so you've become convinced you can't stop until the results come in. The same urgency keeps stacking up, and your body is wearing out first.
merge.F4>G: You burned all your strength trying to see results fast, so your energy hit bottom, and with no results, it became embarrassing to tell anyone. You're worn out and shrinking into yourself alone.
merge.F4>H: Outside schedules and conditions won't move up just because you want them to, yet you've pushed yourself to get results fast. The situation is slow and only your mind is in a hurry, so you're stuck fretting in the gap between them.
merge.F5>A: While you clung to one thing, you couldn't put the other tasks off either, so in the end you took it all on yourself. You're holding on with one hand gripping that one thing and the other carrying everything else.
merge.F5>B: While you were absorbed in one thing, you just went along with everything else, and meanwhile the hurt quietly piled up. One side is full and the other is empty.
merge.F5>C: Because you've been caught up in just one thing, everything else kept getting pushed to “later.” The postponed things have piled up, and now you've stopped, not knowing where to start.
merge.F5>D: The more you've bet everything on one thing, the more the fear has grown that everything will collapse if it wavers. So you sway hard at even small surprises and are barely holding on.
merge.F5>E: You've poured so much into one thing for so long that letting it go feels like losing everything, so you hold on even tighter. The more time you've put in, the harder it is to open your hand, and you're stuck where you are.
merge.F5>F: Your habit of focusing on just one thing meets the pressure to get more done, so you've pushed everything else aside and clung to that one thing. Your body and your life have both worn down on one side.
merge.F5>G: While absorbed in one thing, you forgot how to rest and how to see people. When your energy for it ran out, you were left worn out and alone with no one to lean on.
merge.F5>H: While you focused only on the one side you want, the tasks and conditions coming in from outside kept piling up. What you're holding on to and what you have to do keep clashing, so you can't do either one properly.
merge.G2>A: Even on days off, your mind kept hold of work, and in that state you've taken on other people's shares too. The load you've never once put down has gone past what you can carry alone.
merge.G2>B: Even during your rest, you've been reading the room and going along, so you never truly rested. While you held back and held on, fatigue and hurt have been piling up together.
merge.G2>C: Rest doesn't refresh you, so you have no strength to start what needs doing, and the things you've put off weigh down your rest again. Time just passes while you neither rest nor get things done.
merge.G2>D: Even lying down, your mind kept running through worst cases, so rest never felt like rest. The more tired you get, the bigger the worry gets, and that keeps waking you up again.
merge.G2>E: Even while resting, you kept going over what happened and what you missed, so your mind couldn't rest. You can't open the hand that holds on to it, and fatigue has piled up layer on layer.
merge.G2>F: Rest never really eased your body, and now you're pushing yourself on top of that, so even when you're still, you're racing inside. With no chance to recover, your energy keeps dropping.
merge.G2>G: The tiredness that rest never cleared meets the exhaustion you feel right now, so your body feels twice as heavy. Without even the energy to see people, you're sinking alone.
merge.G2>H: Outside tasks and conditions give you no room to rest, so even your rest time fills up with thoughts of what's next. The situation won't let you go and your body won't loosen, so only the fatigue piles up.
merge.G3>A: Because you've hidden away from people, you have no one to ask for help, so you've ended up handling everything that comes up alone. You're holding on without leaning on anyone.
merge.G3>B: You avoid people, and when you do run into them, you only go along for fear of awkwardness. With even fewer chances to share what you feel, you're swallowing the hurt alone.
merge.G3>C: Hiding alone, you have no one to ask and no one to give you a push, so decisions keep getting put off. Your thoughts just circle on their own, and you haven't decided anything.
merge.G3>D: The more you avoid people, the more afraid you get of being hurt if you reach out again, and that worry sends you deeper into hiding. So you've closed the door and curled up alone.
merge.G3>E: While hiding away alone, you've kept thinking back to people and times from before and holding on to them. You can't let new people in, and you're tied only to what's passed.
merge.G3>F: Even while hiding alone, you've scolded yourself that you can't keep living like this. With no one to lean on and only that harsh inner voice for company, you're wearing down.
merge.G3>G: Your habit of hiding from people has met the exhaustion you feel now, so your time alone has grown longer and harder to break out of. You've started to think talking won't help, and you're left isolated and drained.
merge.G3>H: Things around you are shaky and hard to handle, but you've been hiding from people, so you've had no one to get through it with and no one to ask. Getting through all these changes alone has run your energy down to nothing.
merge.H1>A: Sudden changes taught you there was no one to lean on, so now you try to handle everything yourself. Patching up everything that got shaken, all on your own, has worn you out.
merge.H1>B: When things around you kept shifting, you learned to set aside what you wanted and go along so you wouldn't stir things up. The habit of holding back you picked up then still makes you swallow your words.
merge.H1>C: After a sudden change, you've come to wait until things feel certain, afraid everything will flip again. The memory of everything shaking keeps you from deciding anything right now.
merge.H1>D: Ever since one sudden change, even small news makes you afraid first: “What if it happens again?” The shock from that change keeps making your fears bigger.
merge.H1>E: Because things once shook hard around you, you've started holding even tighter to what little you have left. Afraid of losing more, you can't loosen your grip, and you're stuck where you were.
merge.H1>F: While things kept shifting around you, you pushed yourself harder so you wouldn't fall behind. The tension left over from that still won't let you rest, and it keeps wearing you down.
merge.H1>G: The strength you used up getting through one change after another hasn't come back, and along the way you lost the energy to see people. The outside events are over, but you're left alone and worn out.
merge.H1>H: The sudden changes you went through have come back as new outside pressure, so the shaking hasn't stopped long enough to let you catch your breath. The same kind of blow landing twice has left you with even less room to move.
merge.H4>A: You've been doing what had to be done first and putting off what you wanted, and along the way you decided every task is yours to carry. So even now, you carry it all alone and don't look after your own needs.
merge.H4>B: After so many times of putting what had to be done first, you picked up the habit of thinking “what I want can wait.” Because of that habit, you still go along with others and set aside what you want.
merge.H4>C: You've pushed what you want to the back for so long that now you aren't even sure what it is. So every time you have to choose, you hesitate and end up deciding nothing.
merge.H4>D: What had to be done left you few chances to try what you wanted, so now when you finally go to try it, you're afraid you'll look clumsy. That's why you haven't started yet, and the worry just keeps growing.
merge.H4>E: You regret what you missed out on while doing what had to be done, so you keep looking back at that time. Still holding on to that regret, you can't bring yourself to start what's in front of you.
merge.H4>F: The habit of pushing yourself to get through what had to be done still drives you and won't let you rest. What you want is still pushed to the back, and your energy keeps running lower.
merge.H4>G: All that time you got by doing only what had to be done, you did nothing to fill yourself back up. Now your energy has hit bottom, and there's no one close by to talk to about it.
merge.H4>H: What you wanted kept getting pushed aside by what had to be done, and now outside circumstances are doing the same thing, so the pattern is twice as hard to break. Your own plans get pushed back again, and you're dragged along by a schedule someone else set.
